t: An Ottoman province founded by the Barbarossa brothers, which became a largely self-governing corsair state ruled by elected deys.
Corsairing, captive ransoms and tribute from European states paid for a small Turkish military elite that ruled a mostly rural Maghreb.
It defeated Charles V in 1541 but was crippled by bombardments in 1815–1816 and conquered by France in 1830.
dyk: Miguel de Cervantes spent five years as a captive in Algiers and tried to escape four times before Trinitarian friars ransomed him in 1580.
ev: The corsair Oruç Barbarossa seizes Algiers
Hayreddin Barbarossa places Algiers under the Ottoman sultan and becomes beylerbey
Hayreddin captures the Spanish fort on the Peñón and builds the harbour mole
Charles V’s expedition against Algiers is wrecked by a storm and repulsed
The corsair captains impose the first dey
Algiers takes Oran from Spain, losing it in 1732 and recovering it in 1792
An Anglo-Dutch fleet under Lord Exmouth bombards Algiers
French troops land at Sidi Ferruch and Algiers capitulates on 5 July

f.predecessor: Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen; Hafsid Sultanate
